In summary, our research is concerned with
the modeling and simulation of the radiation effects in MOS transistors and the development of a new compact model of the radiation-induced drain current in MOSFETs.

the development of a compact MOSFETS model that allows us to simulate the total dose dependence of drain currents in irradiated long- and short-channel devices at different measurement temperatures, and the simulation of the OFF-state drain current in the MOSFET irradiated with a high dose.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the presented model is a powerful tool for the analysis of the radiation response of MOSFETs in all operation modes and for the simulation of radiation-induced degradation of the digital circuits.
the proposed model is a very useful and powerful tool for the simulation and analysis of the dose dependent $I-V$ characteristics of irradiated MOS transistors.
the proposed model is capable of predicting the total dose dependencies in the OFF-state and ON-state drain currents in long- and short-channel n-MOSFETS with high accuracy.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the proposed model can be applied in the design and simulation of the radiation-hardened-by-design (RHBD) CMOS integrated circuits.

a new compact MOSFET modeling approach was developed for the simulation of dose-dependent drain currents in the short- and long-channel devices at various measurement temperatures and interface states densities.
the model is able to simulate the drain current in the OFF-state, ON-state, and the transition region between them, and to describe the temperature dependence of the OFF-state drain current.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the model is capable of simulating the drain current dependencies of MOSFETs on the total dose, temperature, interface trap density, and the gate oxide thickness.
the proposed approach allows us to simulate the dose-dependent drain currents of MOSFETs with a single parameter set and a single model equation.
the proposed model can be successfully used in the design of radiation-hardened circuits.
